newsitem.title: UK: Britain's Fergie repays debts, plans smaller home.
newsitem.headline: Britain's Fergie repays debts, plans smaller home.

text.p: Britain's Duchess of York said on Sunday she had cleared a 4.2 million pound ($6.89 million) bank overdraft and planned to move to a smaller house to help pay a 1.6 million pound ($2.62 million) tax bill.

The confirmation in a statement followed press reports that the flamboyant duchess, better known as Fergie from her maiden name Sarah Ferguson, had paid off most of her debts in just four months through a string of lucrative and sometimes embarrassing commercial deals.

"The Duchess of York is pleased to announce that following recent business transactions she has satisfied all her obligations to (bankers) Coutts and Co with regard to her finances," the statement from her office said.
Fergie, former wife of Queen Elizabeth's second son Prince Andrew, was quoted as telling the Sunday Times she had more hard work ahead.
"But I am looking forward to a new period in my life and am approaching it in a positive frame of mind," she told the newspaper.

The Sunday Times said Fergie was planning further drastic cut-backs to her high-spending lifestyle, including a move from her six-bedroomed rented country house to a more modest family home for herself and her two daughters.
She is also expected to cut the number of staff who work for her -- currently more than 10 people including secretaries, nannies and maids.

Fergie had vowed to wipe out her mountainous debts within 12 months and embarked on a series of deals, including a U.S. television advert for cranberry juice and a much-criticised endorsement of Weight Watchers in the United States.

She also received a one million pound advance for her autobiography and was said to have been paid 20,000 pounds for the three hours she spent signing copies in the luxury London department store Harrods.
She won contracts with Paris Match magazines to conduct celebrity interviews for them and her children's books about Budgie the helicopter are being merchandised into toys.
Some of her money-making schemes have raised eyebrows in Britain where members of the royal family have always shunned appearing in adverts.
A source close to the duchess said she still had to pay off 1.6 million pounds in tax bills to the British authorities and wanted to change her lifestyle.
"She is totally serious about downshifting," the source told the Sunday Times. ($1=.6097 Pound)
